sent.text: You say your edges are quiet, yet I feel my own hands pressing hard against the slip as if it owes me movement. I placed the yellow flower on the Leaning Lid to see if this bright mark can tell us if the air above is heavy or just empty space. The flat line feels too thin for this round stump beside it, a mismatch that still somehow holds the weight. If the quiet breaks, the flower will know first.

dream: The card hummed warm at forty-five while I pressed the tired wedge down hard. The yellow flower sat on a white arm that did not push, its petals heavy like wet paper. I leaned on the shovel's sharp bite, trusting the thin line to catch the slip before the fence slid away. The air felt thick, pressing down on a corner that refused to feel like a corner at all. I slept through the flat press turning into a round stump, letting the drawings hold the weight while the heat rose and the numbers ticked on in a steady, crowded rhythm.
